metadata.title: HyperLogLog: the analysis of a near-optimal cardinality estimation algorithm
metadata.authors: Philippe Flajolet, Eric Fusy, Olivier Gandouet, Frederic Meunier
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF->text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Hash function (idealized)
nodes.statement: A hash function $h : D \to \{0,1\}^{\infty}$ assigns to each element of the data domain $D$ an infinite binary string whose bits are independent and each take value $0$ or $1$ with probability $1/2$.
nodes.statement_clean: Hash function mapping data elements to uniformly random infinite bit strings.

nodes.name: Observable
nodes.statement: An observable of a multiset $S \equiv h(\mathcal{M})$ of $\{0,1\}^{\infty}$ strings is a function that depends only on the underlying set of $S$, i.e., a quantity invariant under replications.
nodes.statement_clean: A function of a multiset that ignores duplicate elements.

nodes.name: Leftmost-1-bit position $\rho(s)$
nodes.statement: For $s \in \{0,1\}^{\infty}$, $\rho(s)$ is the position of the leftmost $1$-bit (equivalently, one plus the length of the initial run of $0$'s); e.g., $\rho(0001\cdots) = 4$.
nodes.statement_clean: Position of the leftmost 1-bit in a binary string.

nodes.name: Stochastic averaging
nodes.statement: A technique that emulates $m$ parallel experiments using a single hash function by partitioning the unit interval of hashed values into $m$ equal subintervals indexed by the first $b$ bits, where $m = 2^b$.
nodes.statement_clean: Splitting the hashed stream into m substreams via leading bits to simulate m parallel runs with one hash.

nodes.name: Max-observable per substream
nodes.statement: For substream $\mathcal{N} \equiv \mathcal{M}_j$ (hashed values stripped of their first $b$ bits), the substream observable is $\mathrm{Max}(\mathcal{N}) := \max_{x \in \mathcal{N}} \rho(x)$, with the convention $\mathrm{Max}(\emptyset) = -\infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Per-substream observable: maximum leftmost-1-bit position over hashed values.

nodes.name: HyperLogLog indicator $Z$
nodes.statement: After processing all elements, the indicator is $Z := \bigl( \sum_{j=1}^{m} 2^{-M^{(j)}} \bigr)^{-1}$, where $M^{(j)}$ is the value of $\mathrm{Max}(\mathcal{M}_j)$ stored in register $j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Reciprocal of the sum of 2^{-M[j]}; proportional to the harmonic mean of 2^{M[j]}.

nodes.name: HyperLogLog cardinality estimate $E$
nodes.statement: The HyperLogLog estimate is $E := \dfrac{\alpha_m m^2}{\sum_{j=1}^m 2^{-M^{(j)}}}$, where $\alpha_m := \Bigl( m \int_0^{\infty} \log_2\bigl(\tfrac{2+u}{1+u}\bigr)^m du \Bigr)^{-1}$ is a bias-correction constant.
nodes.statement_clean: Estimator: alpha_m times m^2 times harmonic-mean-like aggregate Z.

nodes.name: Ideal multiset
nodes.statement: An ideal multiset of cardinality $n$ is a sequence obtained by arbitrary replications and permutations of $n$ i.i.d. uniform random variables on the real interval $[0,1]$.
nodes.statement_clean: Multiset modeled as iid Uniform[0,1] variables (with arbitrary repetitions).

nodes.name: Mellin transform
nodes.statement: For $f : \mathbb{R}_{>0} \to \mathbb{C}$, the Mellin transform is $f^{\star}(s) := \int_0^{+\infty} f(t)\, t^{s-1}\, dt$.
nodes.statement_clean: Integral transform mapping a positive-real function to a complex function of s.

nodes.name: Poisson model
nodes.statement: Under the Poisson model of rate $\lambda$, the multiset has a random cardinality $N$ with $P(N=n) = e^{-\lambda} \lambda^n / n!$.
nodes.statement_clean: Replace fixed sample size n by a Poisson(lambda) random size.

nodes.name: Bias-correction constant $\alpha_m$
nodes.statement: $\alpha_m = \Bigl( m \int_0^{\infty} \log_2\!\bigl(\tfrac{2+u}{1+u}\bigr)^m du \Bigr)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Geometric distribution of $\rho$
nodes.statement: Each $Y = \rho(x)$ is geometrically distributed: $P(Y \geq k) = 2^{1-k}$ for $k \geq 1$.

nodes.name: Identity $1/a = \int_0^{\infty} e^{-at} dt$
nodes.statement: $\dfrac{1}{a} = \int_0^{\infty} e^{-at}\, dt$, used to decouple the harmonic-mean factor.

nodes.name: Integral form $H(x)$
nodes.statement: $E_{P(x)}(Z) = H(x/m)$, where $H(x) := x \int_0^{+\infty} G(x, xu)^m du$ and $G(x,t) := \sum_{k \geq 1} g(x/2^k) e^{-t/2^k}$, $g(x) = e^{-x} - e^{-2x}$.

nodes.name: Mellin factorization of $h_u^{\star}(s)$
nodes.statement: $h_u^{\star}(s) = \dfrac{2^s\, \Gamma(s)}{1 - 2^s}\bigl((1+u)^{-s} - (2+u)^{-s}\bigr)$ in the fundamental strip $\langle -1, 0\rangle$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic constants $\alpha_m, \beta_m$
nodes.statement: $\alpha_m \sim \dfrac{1}{2 \log 2} \doteq 0.72134$ and $\beta_m \sim \sqrt{3 \log 2 - 1} \doteq 1.03896$ as $m \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Ideal-multiset hypothesis
nodes.statement: Throughout the analytical Sections 2 and 3, the hashed-value collection $h(\mathcal{M})$ is assumed to constitute an ideal multiset (cf. Definition DP313.8); the number of distinct elements then equals $n$ with probability $1$.

nodes.name: Main theorem: bias and standard error of HyperLogLog
nodes.statement: For HyperLogLog applied to an ideal multiset of cardinality $n$ with $m \geq 3$ registers: (i) $\tfrac{1}{n}\, E_n(E) = 1 + \delta_1(n) + o(1)$ with $|\delta_1(n)| < 5 \cdot 10^{-5}$ when $m \geq 16$; (ii) $\tfrac{1}{n}\sqrt{V_n(E)} = \beta_m/\sqrt{m} + \delta_2(n) + o(1)$ with $|\delta_2(n)| < 5 \cdot 10^{-4}$ when $m \geq 16$, where $\beta_{\infty} = \sqrt{3 \log 2 - 1} \doteq 1.03896$.
nodes.statement_clean: HyperLogLog is asymptotically nearly unbiased and has standard error roughly 1.04/sqrt(m).
assumptions: Algorithm HyperLogLog of Figure 2 is applied
Input is an ideal multiset of cardinality $n$
conclusions: (i) Asymptotically almost unbiased: $\tfrac{1}{n} E_n(E) = 1 + \delta_1(n) + o(1)$ with $|\delta_1(n)| < 5\cdot 10^{-5}$ for $m \geq 16$

nodes.name: Exact expectation of $Z$ (fixed-$n$ model)
assumptions: Ideal multiset of cardinality $n$ split into $m$ submultisets with multinomial sizes
conclusions: Exact formula for $E_n(Z)$ summing over register-value vectors $(k_1,\ldots,k_m)$

nodes.name: Asymptotics of Poisson expectation
nodes.statement: With $\alpha_m$ as in (3), $E_{P(\lambda)}(Z) = \dfrac{\lambda}{m \alpha_m}\bigl(1 + \epsilon_m(\lambda/m) + o(1)\bigr)$ as $\lambda \to \infty$, with $|\epsilon_m(t)| < 5 \cdot 10^{-5}/m$ when $m \geq 16$.
nodes.statement_clean: Under Poisson sampling, the expectation of Z is asymptotically lambda/(m*alpha_m).
assumptions: Number of registers $m \geq 16$ for the explicit numerical bound
conclusions: $E_{P(\lambda)}(Z) \sim \lambda/(m \alpha_m)$ up to a tiny oscillating correction $\epsilon_m$

nodes.name: Mellin asymptotics of $G(x, xu)$
nodes.statement: For each fixed $u > 0$, as $x \to +\infty$: $G(x, xu) = f(u)\bigl(1 + O(x^{-1})\bigr) + \epsilon(x,u)$ for $u \leq 1$, and $G(x, xu) = f(u)\bigl(1 + 2 \widetilde{\epsilon}(x,u) + O(x^{-1})\bigr)$ for $u > 1$, where $f(u) = \log_2\!\bigl(\tfrac{2+u}{1+u}\bigr)$ and $|\epsilon|, |\widetilde{\epsilon}| \leq \epsilon_0 \simeq 7 \cdot 10^{-6}$ for $x \geq 0$.
nodes.statement_clean: Mellin-based asymptotic expansion of the integrand G(x,xu) with tiny uniform error.

nodes.name: Depoissonization of $E_n(Z)$
nodes.statement: $E_n(Z) = E_{P(n)}(Z) + O(1)$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.statement_clean: Fixed-size and Poisson expectations of Z agree up to a bounded error.
assumptions: Analytic-depoissonization conditions $C_1, C_2$ are satisfied for $f(z) = H(z/m)$

nodes.name: Analytic depoissonization (Jacquet-Szpankowski)
nodes.statement: Let $f(z) = e^{-z} \sum f_k z^k/k!$ be the Poisson generating function of $(f_k)$, entire. If there exist a cone $S_{\theta} = \{z = re^{i\varphi}, |\varphi| \leq \theta\}$ with $\theta < \pi/2$ and $\alpha < 1$ such that ($C_1$) $|f(z)| = O(|z|)$ for $z \in S_{\theta}$ and ($C_2$) $|f(z) e^z| = O(e^{\alpha |z|})$ for $z \notin S_{\theta}$, then $f_n = f(n) + O(1)$.
nodes.statement_clean: Saddle-point / cone conditions yielding f_n = f(n) + O(1) for entire Poisson GFs.

nodes.name: Variance integral form $K(x)$
nodes.statement: $E_{P(\lambda)}(Z^2) = K(\lambda/m)$, where $K(x) := x^2 \int_0^{+\infty} u\, G(x, xu)^m du$.

nodes.name: Asymptotic Poisson variance
nodes.statement: $V_{P(\lambda)}(Z) = \lambda^2 \Bigl( \int_0^{\infty} u\, f(u)^m du - \bigl(\int_0^{\infty} f(u)^m du\bigr)^2 + \epsilon''(\lambda) + o(1) \Bigr)$ with $\epsilon''$ small.

nodes.name: Depoissonized variance
nodes.statement: $V_n(Z) = V_{P(n)}(Z) + O(n)$ as $n \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Arithmetic nature of $\alpha_m, \beta_m$
nodes.statement: The integrals $J_0(m), J_1(m)$ that determine $\alpha_m$ and $\beta_m$ are rational combinations of $L = \log 2$, values of $\zeta$ at integers, and polylogarithms at $1/2$; e.g. $J_0(2) = \tfrac{\pi^2}{6 L^2} - 2$, $J_0(3) = \tfrac{3\zeta(3)}{4 L^3} - 2$.

nodes.name: HyperLogLog algorithm
nodes.statement: Single-pass cardinality estimator that maintains $m = 2^b$ registers $M[1\ldots m]$, updates $M[j] := \max(M[j], \rho(w))$ for each item, and returns $E := \alpha_m m^2 / \sum_j 2^{-M[j]}$.
input: Multiset $\mathcal{M}$ of items from a domain $D$ (read sequentially, single pass)
Hash function $h : D \to \{0,1\}^{\infty}$ producing uniform random bits
output: Cardinality estimate $E := \alpha_m m^2 / \sum_{j=1}^m 2^{-M[j]}$ of the number of distinct elements of $\mathcal{M}$

nodes.name: Initialize registers
nodes.statement: Set $M[1], \ldots, M[m] := -\infty$ (in the analytical algorithm) or $0$ (in the practical program of Figure 3).

nodes.name: Stream loop: hash, address, update
nodes.statement: For each $v \in \mathcal{M}$: set $x := h(v)$; let $j := 1 + \langle x_1 x_2 \cdots x_b \rangle_2$ (binary address from first $b$ bits); set $w := x_{b+1} x_{b+2}\cdots$; update $M[j] := \max(M[j], \rho(w))$.

nodes.name: Compute indicator $Z$
nodes.statement: Compute $Z := \bigl( \sum_{j=1}^{m} 2^{-M[j]} \bigr)^{-1}$.

nodes.name: Return estimate
nodes.statement: Return $E := \alpha_m m^2 Z$ with $\alpha_m$ as in equation (3).

nodes.name: HyperLogLog program (with small/large range corrections)
nodes.statement: Practical version: registers initialized to $0$; raw estimate $E$ then post-corrected for small ($E \leq \tfrac{5}{2} m$) and large ($E > \tfrac{1}{30} 2^{32}$) ranges via $m \log(m/V)$ and $-2^{32} \log(1 - E/2^{32})$, respectively.
input: Multiset $\mathcal{M}$ of items from a domain $D$
output: Corrected cardinality estimate $E^{\star}$ with typical relative error $\pm 1.04/\sqrt{m}$, valid for $n$ in range $[0, 10^9]$

nodes.name: Initialize registers to 0
nodes.statement: Initialize $M[1], \ldots, M[m]$ to $0$ (instead of $-\infty$) so that small-cardinality estimates remain usable.

nodes.name: Streaming update loop
nodes.statement: For each $v \in \mathcal{M}$: $x := h(v)$; $j := 1 + \langle x_1\cdots x_b\rangle_2$; $w := x_{b+1} x_{b+2}\cdots$; $M[j] := \max(M[j], \rho(w))$.

nodes.name: Compute raw estimate $E$
nodes.statement: Compute $E := \alpha_m m^2 \cdot \bigl( \sum_{j=1}^m 2^{-M[j]} \bigr)^{-1}$ (raw HyperLogLog estimate).

nodes.name: Range-dependent correction
nodes.statement: If $E \leq \tfrac{5}{2} m$: let $V$ be the number of zero registers; if $V \neq 0$ set $E^{\star} := m \log(m/V)$ else $E^{\star} := E$ (small-range, linear-counting correction). If $\tfrac{5}{2} m < E \leq \tfrac{1}{30} 2^{32}$: $E^{\star} := E$ (intermediate range). If $E > \tfrac{1}{30} 2^{32}$: $E^{\star} := -2^{32} \log(1 - E/2^{32})$ (large-range hash-collision correction).

nodes.name: Return corrected estimate
nodes.statement: Return cardinality estimate $E^{\star}$ with typical relative error $\pm 1.04/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: LogLog (Durand-Flajolet)
nodes.statement: Cardinality estimator using $m$ registers of $\leq 5$ bits with relative accuracy $1.30/\sqrt{m}$, based on the same bit-pattern observable $\rho$ but using a geometric-mean evaluator.
output: Cardinality estimate with typical relative error $1.30/\sqrt{m}$

nodes.name: Probabilistic Counting (Flajolet-Martin)
nodes.statement: Bit-pattern-based cardinality estimator using $m$ words ($\leq 32$ bits each) with relative accuracy $0.78/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: MinCount
nodes.statement: Order-statistics-based cardinality estimator (smallest hashed values) using $m$ words with relative accuracy $1.00/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: Adaptive Sampling
nodes.statement: Cardinality estimator using $m$ words ($\approx 32$ bits each) with relative accuracy $1.20/\sqrt{m}$.

nodes.name: Hit Counting (Whang et al.)
nodes.statement: Linear-time probabilistic counting using a bitmap of $\approx N/10$ bits with $\approx 2\%$ accuracy; the count of empty bins $V$ relates to cardinality via $n \approx m \log(m/V)$.

nodes.name: Cardinality estimation of a streamed multiset
nodes.statement: Given a (possibly very large) data stream $\mathcal{M}$ from a domain $D$, estimate the cardinality $n = |\mathrm{set}(\mathcal{M})|$ in a single pass using sublinear (typically $O(\log \log N)$ per register) auxiliary memory.

nodes.name: Memory $\log_2 \log_2 N + O(1)$ bits per register
nodes.statement: HyperLogLog needs registers of at most $\log_2 \log_2 N + O(1)$ bits to estimate cardinalities $\leq N$; with $m = 2048$, 32-bit hashing, and 5-bit registers, $n$ up to $> 10^9$ is estimated at $\approx 2\%$ accuracy using $\approx 1.5$ kB.

nodes.name: Optimal parallelization / sliding window
nodes.statement: Given an arbitrary partition of the input file, register vectors can be combined componentwise by $\max$, yielding optimal parallel/distributed implementation; the algorithm also adapts to the sliding-window model.

nodes.name: Information-theoretic lower bound $\Omega(\log\log N)$
nodes.statement: Maintaining $\epsilon$-approximate counts up to $N$ necessitates $\Omega(\log \log N)$ bits, since cardinalities lie on an exponential scale $1, (1+\epsilon), \ldots, (1+\epsilon)^L = N$ requiring $\log_2 \log_{1+\epsilon} N$ bits.

nodes.name: Lower bound from order-statistics class
nodes.statement: For a wide class of order-statistics-based cardinality estimators, the best achievable accuracy is bounded below by a quantity close to $1/\sqrt{m}$; HyperLogLog is within about $4\%$ of this information-theoretic optimum.

nodes.name: Real-life test on Analytic Combinatorics PostScript dump
nodes.statement: With $m = 2048$ (predicted standard error $\pm 2\%$), HyperLogLog was run on $458$ chunks of $\approx 40{,}000$ lines each obtained from octal dumps of the PostScript source of the book Analytic Combinatorics; the empirical relative-error histogram closely matches the theoretical Gaussian.

nodes.name: Simulations on ideal multisets
nodes.statement: Traces of four typical executions on ideal random multisets for $\langle N, m \rangle \in \{ \langle 10^4, 256\rangle, \langle 10^7, 1024\rangle, \langle 10^8, 1024\rangle, \langle 10^7, 65536\rangle\}$ confirm relative errors within the predicted $\pm 1.04/\sqrt{m}$ band, and 500/250 simulations at $(n,m) = (10^4, 256), (10^6, 1024)$ produce empirical histograms approximated by Gaussians.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP313.2 (Mellin asymptotics of Poisson expectation)
nodes.statement: By integral representation (9) of the Poisson expectation, Mellin analysis of the integrand $G(x, xu)$ (Lemma LP313.1), and integration over $u \in [0,1]$ and $u \in [1, \infty)$ to extract the dominant term $H(x) = x \bigl( \int_0^{\infty} f(u)^m du + \epsilon_m(x) + o(1) \bigr)$.

nodes.name: Integral representation via $1/a = \int_0^{\infty} e^{-at} dt$
nodes.statement: Apply the identity $1/a = \int_0^{\infty} e^{-at} dt$ to the harmonic factor $(\sum 2^{-k_j})^{-1}$, separating variables and producing $E_{P(mx)}(Z) = \int_0^{\infty} G(x,t)^m dt$ (Equation EP313.4).

nodes.name: Mellin analysis of integrand
nodes.statement: Apply Lemma LP313.1 to $h_u(x) = G(x, xu)$, using factorization $h_u^{\star}(s) = 2^s \Gamma(s) ((1+u)^{-s} - (2+u)^{-s})/(1 - 2^s)$ in the strip $\langle -1, 0\rangle$, and bound the residue series and remainder integral.

nodes.name: Split integral $A + B$ and bound on $[0,1], [1, \infty)$
nodes.statement: Split $\frac{1}{x} H(x) = A + B + o(1)$ with $A = \int_0^1$ and $B = \int_1^{\infty}$. Use $f(u) \leq 1 - 2u/5$ on $[0,1]$ and $f(u) \leq 1/((1+u)\log 2)$ on $[1, \infty)$ to get $|A - \int_0^1 f^m| \leq 6.26\, \epsilon_0/(m+1)$ and $|B - \int_1^{\infty} f^m| \leq \tfrac{2}{m-1} \bigl((1+2\epsilon_0)^m - 1\bigr)/(2 \log 2)^m$.

nodes.name: Conclude $H(x) = x ( \int_0^{\infty} f(u)^m du + \epsilon_m(x) + o(1))$
nodes.statement: Combine the bounds on $A$ and $B$ with Equation (9) to obtain $H(x) = x\bigl(\int_0^{\infty} f(u)^m du + \epsilon_m(x) + o(1)\bigr)$ with $|\epsilon_m(x)| < 5 \cdot 10^{-5}/m$ for $m \geq 16$, finishing Proposition PrP313.2.

nodes.name: Proof of Proposition PrP313.3 (depoissonization of $E_n(Z)$)
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem TP313.2 (analytic depoissonization) to $f(z) := H(z/m)$ with cone half-angle $\theta = \pi/3$ and $\alpha = 3/5$; verify conditions $C_1$ inside and $C_2$ outside the cone using bounds on $G(z/m, t)$ revisited from the Mellin analysis.

nodes.name: Verify $C_1$ inside cone
nodes.statement: For $z = r e^{i\varphi}$ with $|\varphi| \leq \pi/3$: $|z^{-s}| = r^{-\sigma} e^{\tau \varphi}$ stays controlled within the cone; the residue series in (13) and the remainder integral remain $O(1)$, so Lemma LP313.1 extends and $H(z) = O(|z|)$, hence $H(z/m) = O(|z|)$.

nodes.name: Verify $C_2$ outside cone, case $\Re(z) < 0$
nodes.statement: Set $L := \lfloor \log_2(|z|/m) \rfloor$, split the sum defining $G(z/m, t)$ at $k = L$, use $(X+Y)^m \leq 2^m X^m + 2^m Y^m$ and the convergent integral $\Gamma_m := \int_0^{\infty} (\sum_k 2^{-k} e^{-t/2^k})^m dt$ to bound $|H(z/m)| \leq A e^{-z} z \log_2|z|^m + B|z^m|$, hence $|e^z H(z/m)| = O(e^{\alpha |z|})$ with $\alpha = 3/5$.

nodes.name: Verify $C_2$ outside cone, case $\Re(z) \geq 0$
nodes.statement: For $\Re(z) \geq 0$ outside the cone: $|G(z/m, t)| \leq |z| \sum_k 2^{-k} e^{-t/2^k}$, so $|H(z/m)| \leq |z|^m \Gamma_m$; since $\Re(z) < |z|/2$ outside the cone, $|e^z H(z/m)| = O(e^{|z|/2} z^m) = O(e^{3|z|/5})$.

nodes.name: Conclude $E_n(Z) = E_{P(n)}(Z) + O(1)$
nodes.statement: By Theorem TP313.2 with $C_1, C_2$ both verified, $f_n = f(n) + O(1)$ where $f(z) = H(z/m)$, i.e., $E_n(Z) = E_{P(n)}(Z) + O(1)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem TP313.1 (sketch)
nodes.statement: Combine Propositions PrP313.2 (Poisson asymptotics of $E(Z)$) and PrP313.3 (depoissonization) for part (i); for part (ii), repeat the parallel analysis on $E(Z^2)$ via integral $K(x)$ and depoissonize to get $V_n(Z) = V_{P(n)}(Z) + O(n)$, then bound $\beta_m$ via the integrals $J_0(m), J_1(m)$ in Section 3.2.
